shared_preconditions: Before each run, inspect the exact loaded extension ID, version, and Loaded from path in chrome://extensions; reload that extension and record the completed reload. For a case with warm and reload dimensions, execute and record a warm run first without an immediately preceding extension reload, then click Reload for the same extension and execute a separate post-reload run. Reopen the tested surface after each extension reload. A page refresh or reopening a panel alone does not count as extension reload. Apply the case-specific entrypoint route below; the route is conditional by case and build variant.

Use only the existing identity mode(s) listed for the case. Record visible account email and role evidence without credentials. Never change account roles. For authenticated writes, record the active device organization and use synthetic disposable profile values; preserve original values and restore them after each run.

For every execution-matrix row, enter a separate observed outcome and evidence reference. Leave unsupported or unexecuted rows unverified; a missing device, unprovisioned fault, or absent fixture does not pass a branch.

preconditions: Use guest profile as applicable, plus a disposable Chrome profile or known test machine where microphone permission can be reset. Record Chrome site-permission state and whether an input device is connected.

Each matrix row resets and records the extension-origin microphone permission independently. A no-device row is unverified if the approved environment cannot confirm zero available audio inputs; do not substitute a permission denial.
steps: Open Chat and click the microphone control to open the extension mic-grant popup.
Grant path: with permission unset and a working input device, click Allow microphone and accept Chrome’s prompt. Record prompt, page status, popup close timing, and Chat mic state.
Deny path: reset extension-origin microphone permission, repeat and deny the Chrome prompt; record status text and whether retry remains enabled.

No-device path: use a test environment with no available input device and permission allowed, repeat; record visible status. Do not report a scenario as exercised if the environment did not support it.
expected: Grant reports “Granted! Closing…” and closes after roughly 1.5 seconds; denial displays permission-denied recovery guidance and leaves Allow enabled; no device displays no-microphone guidance. Separate outcomes per scenario.
gaps: Inventory bundles three outcomes into one case; it does not specify whether one execution may satisfy it. Do not mark complete until each environment-supported branch has independent evidence.

expected: Browser permission prompt appears; grant reports success, deny reports refusal, missing device reports no-device remedy.
